scope: v2: recommendation consistency + tone + sample-vs-total + hedged-vs-asserted

findings.message: The Priority 3 'What to change and why' bullets switch from first-person ('We confirmed') used throughout the Findings section to third-person passive in the final bullet ('Delivering both headers through a centralised server or CDN configuration ensures consistent cover'), breaking voice mid-section.
findings.context: Deliver both headers through a centralised server or CDN configuration rather than per-page changes, so the fix applies consistently

findings.message: The Priority 5 finding states that 'all five well-known discovery artefacts … are absent' as a site-wide assertion, but absence was confirmed only for the 7 audited pages/fetches, not across the full 51-URL estate declared in the sitemap.
findings.context: All five well-known discovery artefacts we check, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, agent-card.json, ai.txt, and humans.txt, are absent.

findings.message: The Security Headers section asserts that HSTS and CSP are 'absent from every audited response' but the narrative summary in Priority 3 escalates this to a site-wide claim ('Content-Security-Policy and Referrer-Policy absent across all 7 audited URLs'), while the Security Headers table omits HSTS entirely and instead lists Referrer-Policy as the second missing header, creating an internal inconsistency that implies a broader, unscoped claim.
findings.context: We found that 2 of the five standard security headers are absent from every audited response: HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security) and Content-Security-Policy (CSP).

findings.message: The Structured Data Findings section asserts 'Site has no top-level author/owner declared' and 'Site has no logo / hero image declared in structured data' for WebSite entities as site-wide facts, but these are observed only across the 7 audited pages with no hedge limiting the claim to the sample.
findings.context: Site has no logo / hero image declared in structured data … Site has no top-level author/owner declared
